title: Messaging: Kafka, RabbitMQ and managed queues

videos.script: Lesson 5 said a message waits somewhere until its receiver is ready. This lesson is about that somewhere. {{broker}} There are two kinds of broker, and they are built on two different ideas. {{two}} A queue hands each message to one consumer and forgets it once it is acknowledged. RabbitMQ is the best known. {{queue}} A log keeps every message in order, for days, and lets each reader keep its own place in it. Kafka is the best known. {{log}} You will run both on your machine. You will publish an event to RabbitMQ before anybody is listening, and watch it disappear. {{lost}} You will write to a Kafka topic with three partitions, and see that order is kept for each customer, and not across them. {{partitions}} And you will read the same topic twice, with two groups that do not know about each other, and then rewind one of them. {{replay}} At the end, the managed versions the cloud providers sell, and a table for choosing. One warning before you start: this lesson runs two brokers at once, so give your machine the 8 GB lesson 1 asked for.
